name: Background Optical Flow
description: Analyzes optical flow consistency in background regions — AI-generated backgrounds often exhibit unrealistic motion patterns or temporal incoherence.
mechanism:
This method analyzes the optical flow field in background regions to detect AI-generated or manipulated video:

1. **Foreground-Background Segmentation and Flow Estimation**: The method separates foreground (moving objects, people) from background using a combination of semantic segmentation and motion-based separation. Dense optical flow is computed on consecutive frame pairs using RAFT (Teed & Deng, 2020). For authentic handheld camera footage, the background optical flow should be consistent with a single rigid camera motion (translation + rotation), describable by the epipolar geometry. The method fits a fundamental matrix to background flow vectors using RANSAC and measures the proportion of inliers. In authentic video, > 90% of background flow vectors are consistent with the fundamental matrix. AI-generated video often shows flow inconsistencies in the background where different regions appear to move independently.

2. **Background Temporal Coherence**: In authentic video, static background elements maintain their relative positions and appearance across frames — they are warped by camera motion but not created or destroyed. The method tracks background feature points across 10-frame windows and checks for temporal consistency: (a) tracked points should have smooth trajectories without teleportation, (b) point appearance (BRIEF descriptors) should change minimally between adjacent frames. AI-generated video frequently shows background temporal instability — textures that flicker, shift, or morph between frames, especially in peripheral regions outside the model's attention focus.

3. **Parallax Consistency with Scene Depth**: Camera translation creates motion parallax — nearby objects move more than distant objects. The method estimates relative depth from the magnitude of optical flow after removing the rotational component. In authentic video, the depth ordering from parallax should be spatially coherent and consistent with scene geometry (ground plane, walls, sky). AI-generated backgrounds often violate parallax: distant objects may move as fast as nearby ones, or the implied depth map contains physically impossible configurations (e.g., surfaces that are both near and far).

4. **Background Flow Noise Analysis**: Authentic video has optical flow estimation noise proportional to scene complexity and motion magnitude. The method analyzes the residual flow (observed flow minus fitted rigid motion model) in homogeneous background regions. In authentic video, this noise follows a zero-mean distribution with variance proportional to image gradient magnitude. AI-generated video shows structured residual patterns — correlated flow errors that form coherent patterns rather than random noise, indicating that the motion was synthesized rather than captured.
parameters:
Optical flow method: RAFT
Segmentation: DeepLabV3+ or Mask R-CNN
Fundamental matrix estimation: RANSAC (threshold = 1.5 px)
Inlier ratio threshold: > 90%
Feature tracking window: 10 frames
BRIEF descriptor size: 256 bits
Parallax depth estimation: translation-compensated flow magnitude
Residual flow analysis block: 16×16 pixels
Minimum background area: 30% of frame
Minimum video length: 30 frames
accuracy: 77–85% accuracy detecting AI-generated video via background flow analysis. Rigid motion consistency achieves AUC of 0.83 for detecting non-physical background motion. Temporal coherence achieves F1-score of 0.80 for identifying background flicker. Parallax consistency analysis most effective for scenes with camera translation (precision = 0.86). Performance decreases for static-camera videos where background flow is near-zero.
source: Teed, Z. & Deng, J. (2020). RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow. Proceedings of ECCV, 402–419.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated video with unrealistic background motion. Identifying green-screen compositing where foreground and background have inconsistent camera motion. Verifying authenticity of surveillance footage. Detecting deepfake videos where the background shows temporal instability.
strengths:
• Background flow should obey rigid geometry — strong physical constraint
• Parallax analysis provides depth-based verification independent of appearance
• Temporal coherence catches flicker artifacts common in current AI video generators
• Residual flow analysis detects subtle structured motion artifacts
• Works on any video with camera motion — does not require faces or people
limitations:
• Static camera videos produce minimal background flow — limited analysis signal
• Moving background objects (trees in wind, traffic) violate the rigid motion assumption
• Very high-quality AI video generators (Sora, Gen-3) are improving background consistency
• Severe compression destroys flow field precision in low-quality video
• Requires reliable foreground-background segmentation as a prerequisite
